definitions.explanation: The practice of giving an old item (typically a car, appliance, or electronic device) to a seller to reduce the price of a new purchase.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}い{車|くるま}を{下取|したど}りに{出|だ}す。
examples.english: To trade in an old car.

examples.japanese: {下取|したど}り{価格|かかく}は{思|おも}ったより{高|たか}かった。
examples.english: The trade-in price was higher than I expected.

examples.japanese: スマホを{買|か}い{替|か}えるとき、{今|いま}の{機種|きしゅ}を{下取|したど}りしてもらえるか{聞|き}いてみた。
examples.english: When replacing my smartphone, I asked if they could take my current model as a trade-in.

notes:
USAGE:
{下取|したど}り is most commonly used when buying cars, electronics, and appliances. The seller evaluates the old item and deducts its value from the new purchase price.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {下取|したど}りに{出|だ}す (to trade in, to offer as a trade-in)
- {下取|したど}り{価格|かかく} (trade-in price/value)
- {下取|したど}りしてもらう (to have something accepted as a trade-in)
- {下取|したど}り{査定|さてい} (trade-in appraisal)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{買|か}い{取|と}り means buyback or purchase, where the store buys your item outright. {下取|したど}り specifically implies exchanging an old item when purchasing a new one.
